sir-michael-snyder-building.title: Sir Michael Snyder Building
paragraphs: This project for a new boarding house was completed in 2025 and continues our 20-year relationship with Brentwood School, creating a welcome addition to the campus. The brief consolidates boys’ and girls’ accommodation, previously located on separate sites, expanding the current capacity of 65 to over 120 boarders.

At the southern entry point to Brentwood and overlooking Shenfield Common, the facilities create a much-improved social experience for boarders, focusing on issues of wellbeing through well-designed environments. The building integrates 123 study bedrooms, all with en-suite shower facilities, alongside a communal dining room, kitchens, separate staﬀ accommodation and dedicated landscaped social space.

The new block was built to exacting environmental standards. Underneath the brick skin, a composite structure was adopted to reduce overall embodied carbon: CLT was used to form the cellular study bedrooms of the upper storeys while a concrete podium slab spans the larger communal spaces at ground floor level. This approach was echoed in the building services which are fossil fuel free, utilizing mechanical ventilation and heat recovery throughout, with air-source heat pumps served from a separate curved brick energy station formed adjacent.

lucy-xinlei-guo.title: Lucy (Xinlei) Guo
paragraphs: Lucy joined Cottrell & Vermeulen in 2026.

She completed her RIBA Part I at The University of Sydney, graduating with distinction. After completing her Part I, Lucy worked at Make Architects in Sydney, contributing to a range of residential and commercial projects.
Lucy went on to complete her RIBA Part II at The University of Edinburgh, where she was nominated for University 3DReid Prize.

Since joining CVA, Lucy has worked on a new primary school for London Borough of Brent and is currently involved in the design of a new SEN boarding house and SEN short-stay unit for London Borough of Hounslow.Lucy is fluent in English and Mandarin.

anya-heath.title: Anya Heath
paragraphs: Anya joined Cottrell & Vermeulen in 2026.

Prior to joining CVA, she worked at IID Architects for four years — initially while completing her architectural studies, and subsequently for two years as a qualified architect. During her time there, Anya worked on school projects across all RIBA work stages, as well as a school campus masterplan.Earlier in her career, Anya worked as an architectural assistant at AMA Chartered Architects between 2017–2018 and 2020–2021.Anya studied architecture at the University of Nottingham, where she graduated with a First-Class Master’s degree.Since joining CVA, she has been working as the project architect on the extensive redevelopment of a boatyard on the Thames in Southwark.

yasmine-dahim-2.title: Yasmine Dahim
paragraphs: Yasmine joined Cottrell & Vermeulen in 2022.

Yasmine studied for her RIBA Part I at University of Nottingham where she received a 2:1. Prior to joining the practice Yasmine worked at Apteriors as an FF&E designer on numerous school buildings. Since joining the practice, Yasmine as a part 1 architectural assistant has worked on a new Hindu temple in Harrow, a new school library in Southwark and a renovation project for a boatyard located along the river Thames.

Following her part 1 placement she went on to complete her master’s at Loughborough University graduating with a first-class degree and returning to Cottrell and Vermeulen as a part 2 architectural assistant.
Yasmine is fluent in English and Kabyle.

charter-school-bermondsey.title: Charter School Bermondsey
paragraphs: This new home for a local 4FE secondary school forms the gateway the Bermondsey Project, one of London’s largest build-to-rent developments.

Through a collaborative, school-led process, the project entailed a deep rethink of movement and teaching to facilitate a house-based model across six floors, with highly prominent public frontages. The innovative design had to be reversible to a departmental model and required very close consultation with Grosvenor, the Education Funding Agency, planning and conservation, the existing school, two successive masterplan architects and the local community. We also worked with an educationalist.

The project makes extensive use of colour, pattern and texture to articulate the massing, function and entrances, and includes a shared public landscape. The scheme evolved through extensive change of both masterplan and site, and the confident final design is testament to our collaborative and flexible consultation process, working stringent Education Funding Agency and planning requirements into a contextual language that celebrates the school at the heart of its community.
The school was successfully delivered from Stage 4 by a subsequent EFA-procured, contractor-led team.

st-thomas-the-apostle-school-sixth-form-.title: St Thomas The Apostle School & Sixth Form College Library
paragraphs: A new modular library shapes a social and learning landscape and provides much needed new personal study space and learning resource at the heart of the school, with a form and expression that is playfully contextual to the arched facade of the original chapel and the brick colonnade of the more recent BSF extension.

A ‘bespoke modular’ approach was integral to the viability of delivering the project without a decant. Steel framed, partially clad modules were craned in and completed in the summer holidays, with landscaping works completed at the start of term. The system allowed us to develop a playful language of form, colour and materiality using three brick colours and a solid burnt pink coating for the arched motif and windows.

Finely tuned considerations such as how the landscaping met the buildings and the introduction of an external colonnade makes the project transcend the assumptions of what a modular project should and could look like.

planning-approved-for-new-library.title: Planning Approved for New Library
paragraphs: We are happy that the proposed new library and 6th form study space for St. Thomas the ApostleSchool in Nunhead has received planning permission. The new modular space starts on site in Juneand should be ready for occupation in In September this year providing much needed study spacefor the 6th formers at the school.

ik-hui-lam.title: Romain Rihouet
paragraphs: Romain joined Cottrell & Vermeulen in 2023. Prior to this, he worked at Mahoco Design as a RIBA Part II architectural assistant and worked with Squire & Partners during his RIBA Part I internship in 2019/2020.
Romain completed his degree in architecture at the Architectural Association.
Since joining CVA Romain has been working on new boarding accommodation building for Brentwood School and the refurbishment of the University of Cambridge’s Churchill College campus buildings.

riba-east-award-2022-winners-best-buildi.title: RIBA East Award 2022 winners – Best Building of the Year
paragraphs: The postgraduate housing on Storey’s Way for Churchill College, Cambridge was among 17 projects in the Eastern Region to win an RIBA regional award and we are delighted that it has also been chosen as RIBA East Building of the Year.

st-chads-student-housing.title: St Chads Student Housing
paragraphs: The housing provides 23 additional student rooms at St Chads site for St Catharine’s College.
The site is within a conservation area with established mature trees, a Grade II listed building and 1970’s student accommodation.

A 1970’s building is being demolished and replacing with two new buildings with en-suite student rooms and shared facilities. The organisation of the accommodation has been developed through conversations with students who have lived on the St Chads site.

The architectural approach has been developed from an understanding and response to the existing context of the Conservation Area and the existing architecture of the St Chads site. The character of the Conservation Area is typified by large Arts and Crafts and Queen Anne Houses. The architectural approach of the new buildings reflects the materials and character of the surrounding Conservation Area. The design looks to learn from the details and character of the surrounding architecture, reinterpreted in a contemporary way with a focus on quality and sustainability.
The project was successfully completed in 2023.

riba-east-award-2022-winners.title: RIBA East Award 2022 winners
paragraphs: We are very happy to announce that two of our recent projects have received a 2022 RIBA East Award.

Our graduate housing for Churchill College, Cambridge where the judges noted that ‘The resulting scheme showcases the practice’s experience with graduate housing with great virtuosity’; and our project for Brentwood Preparatory School where the judges noted that ‘The materials palette references other buildings around the site and each building is beautifully crafted with bold and playful colours and motifs’

brentwood-school-reception.title: Brentwood School Reception
paragraphs: The Reception Project for Brentwood School provides a new public space for the school and its visitors. Previously entry to the school was circuitous and disorientating and gave no sense of the its character and history. By removing a number of dysfunctional structures we created a space of arrival and orientation. At the same time, a number of historic school buildings were brought into greater visibility.

The scheme is organised around two principal spaces. A landscaped courtyard, enclosed by the existing Edwardian arcade which connects the public entrance with the main reception. This space is focused on the newly revealed east end of the Victorian school chapel. In the reception space a large wooden skylight precisely frames a view of the stained glass east window, whilst curtain walling gives views of the school garden-landscape beyond.
The two themes of history and landscape which characterise Brentwood School are then complemented by a display wall incorporating school art works and videos.

churchill-college.title: Churchill College, Cambridge
paragraphs: Three new postgraduate houses have recently been completed on a site adjoining the housing completed by CVA in 2002. The new housing is part of an overall masterplan to consolidate a graduate ‘campus within a campus’ for the College.

The architectural approach builds upon the ideas of the original scheme, in responding to the overlapping contexts of the original Sheppard Robson college buildings and the Arts and Crafts character of Storey’s Way.
The college accommodation is split between three new houses, including 30 en-suite student rooms, 6 communal kitchens, 5 self-contained flats and associated support spaces.

The flats consist of 5 student rooms to each communal room. These are clustered on the upper floors of Houses 1 and 2 and ground and first floor of House 3. In addition, the ground floor of Houses 1 and 2 accommodates the independently accessed self-contained flats and support accommodation.

brentwood-preparatory-school-expansion.title: Brentwood Preparatory School Expansion
paragraphs: The project for the Preparatory School was completed in 2020 and continues our 15 year relationship with Brentwood School. The brief included an expansion in the school role, an upgrading of the existing facilities and also presented an opportunity to reorganise the entire site. The site was constrained by the green belt and is within the setting of the listed Middleton Hall.

The new masterplan is structured around a central spine to the site and connects new and refurbished buildings, landscape, play-spaces and carparking. A new hall building provides a flexible facility for assembly, dining and performance. A new classroom block provides a new reception and administration facilities at ground floor as part of a new security strategy for the site. The upper floors house a cluster of cutting-edge, specialist teaching facilities and include a ‘Futures Room’ which provides a space for interdisciplinary projects.
The buildings both draw upon the history of the site and regional typologies, whilst interpreting them through a contemporary and playful architecture.

southwark-architect-design-services-fram.title: Southwark Architect Design Services Framework
paragraphs: We are honoured to be included on this new framework in the categories of Education / Social Care / Community (£5-£20M) and New Homes (£0-£5M). Southwark is home to our offices, a number of our prominent projects, our London Met student work as well as our local work experience students.
We really look forward to this opportunity to continue to engage with Southwark communities and to help them shape sustainable and inclusive spaces for living, learning and socialising.

southwark-schools-work-experience.title: Southwark Schools Work Experience
paragraphs: Through our long standing partnerships with Southwark state schools, we offer early career exposure to aspiring architects of all backgrounds in our local community. During one or two weeks, students develop an independent mini project for a work/social/storage space for our team in Iliffe Yard. This introduces them to key architectural tasks such as brief setting, surveying, researching, drawing, model making and presentation, and gives them a chance to test their skills in both creative and technical areas to inform and inspire future career choices.
This selection of work is drawn from the last decade and celebrates the participants of our work experience programme.

fundraising-drive-launched-for-new-cottr.title: Fundraising drive launched for new Cottrell and Vermeulen-designed community hub in Essex
paragraphs: A fundraising initiative has been launched to turn our new design for Saint Stephen’s Church in Southend-on-Sea into reality, with the church targeting £50,000 to achieve planning permission to build. Colin Baldwin, the Priest-in-charge at St Stephen’s, will stage a 1,000 miles cycle in 10 days this July as part of the drive, visiting the majority of cathedrals in the south and midlands of England.

The new centre will replace the church’s existing dilapidated facilities, and uses modular design to create a building that is flexible and can be easily expanded further in the future as the community’s needs evolve and funding becomes available.
To help the project and donate to Rev. Baldwin’s charity cycle, simply text COLB58 £(amount) to 70070, or alternatively visit the following JustGiving page:
https://www.justgiving.com/fundraising/colinsbaldwin1000

completion-of-krishna-avanti-primary-sch.title: Completion of Krishna Avanti Primary School, Croydon
paragraphs: Our school project in Croydon for the Avanti School Trust and Kier Construction, Krishna Avanti Primary School, has now completed.
The new build two-form entry primary school is a Hindu faith free school open to all, regardless of faith, and is the third development we have designed for the trust.
Having received planning in March 2017 and commenced on site later that year in September, the building features a linear teaching block, double height hall space and a roof top play deck.

krishna-avanti-primary-school-2.title: Krishna Avanti Primary School
paragraphs: Krishna Avanti Primary School is a new build, two form entry primary school in Croydon. It is a Hindu faith free school open to all, regardless of faith.
The school is the third Cottrell and Vermeulen has designed for the trust, of which includes the Krishna Avanti Primary School in Harrow, completed in 2008.
The Croydon school is located on a prominent site in Croydon and the leafy Waldrons Conservation Area. These conditions have strongly influenced the design.
The building features a linear teaching block, double height hall space and a roof top play deck.
The scheme received planning permission in March 2017 and commenced on site later that year in September.

new-yorks-architectural-record-features-.title: New York’s Architectural Record features Cottrell & Vermeulen
paragraphs: American publication Architectural Record has featured Streatham and Clapham High School in a special article focussing upon exemplary vertical school expansions from around the globe.

Our extension and refurbishment – staged over two phases for the Girls’ Day School Trust – was the only UK design to be selected for the article, of which also included outstanding projects from Berlin and New York.
The article has been published in the title’s January 2019 issue and you can also read it online by clicking the link below:
https://www.architecturalrecord.com/articles/13826-continuing-education-vertical-school-expansions

civic-trust-awards-2019-shortlists-belle.title: Civic Trust Awards 2019 shortlists Bellenden Primary School
paragraphs: We are delighted to share that Bellenden Primary School has been shortlisted by the Civic Trust Awards 2019 for the Selwyn Goldsmith Awards for Universal Design.
The Civic Trust Awards recognise buildings and schemes in which are architecturally outstanding and make positive differences to their local community.
All winning schemes will be presented with their award or commendation at the 60th Annual Civic Trust Awards Ceremony, held at the Imperial War Museum North in Manchester on Friday 1st March 2019.

bellenden-primary-school-shortlisted-for.title: Bellenden Primary School shortlisted for AJ Architecture Awards
paragraphs: We are delighted to be shortlisted for School Project of the Year for Bellenden Primary School in the AJ Architecture Awards.
The awards celebrate the very best projects built in the UK and all winners will be announced at the Roundhouse in London on 4th December.

grove-lane-2.title: Grove Lane
paragraphs: Grove Lane is a new two-storey home constructed by Cottrell and Vermeulen Architecture within the Camberwell Grove Conservation Area.

The new development has replaced an existing garage facing onto a mews street, and is both contemporary and simple in form, which also harmonises with neighbouring properties. Large first-floor windows are similar in scale to the neighbouring house, while minimal openings to the ground floor garage maintain privacy from the street. Rich textured stock brick and ‘waney-edge’ timber panelling combine to form a simple yet interesting facade.

Alongside the new building, Cottrell and Vermeulen Architecture has also refurbished and remodelled the main existing Georgian house to make it function better for the residents. The front facade of the historic property has been refurbished, while excavation and remodelling of the front garden provide improved access and daylight at the basement level.

takaungu-creek.title: Takaungu Creek
paragraphs: Located on Takaungu Creek above the mangrove tree tops, this residential development is arranged around a protected courtyard to create an informal domestic setting for a main two-storey house and two single-storey cottages. Employing local materials and traditional building techniques, the un-faced coral block both internally and externally results in a building faithful to the simplicity of the local village houses. The building is ‘off grid’, using renewable energy and collected rainwater and is orientated to maximise sea breezes. A ‘natural’ landscape is being established using indigenous species trees and shrubs to reduce maintenance requirements and to provide a protected  wildlife corridor for suni antelope, sunbirds, elephant shrew and Sykes’ monkeys. The courtyard provides a more manicured landscape and shade protection.

aj-retrofit-awards-2018-school-project-o.title: AJ Retrofit Awards 2018 – School Project of the Year
paragraphs: We are thrilled to have won School Project of the Year for our project Streatham and Clapham High School at the AJ Retrofit Awards 2018.

The judging panel commented on their decision: “The jury liked the energy and ambition of the scheme and how it succeeded in reinvigorating the school campus, re-orientating it to the street and thereby transforming its relationship with the surrounding locality.”

cottrell-and-vermeulen-project-shortlist.title: Cottrell and Vermeulen project shortlisted for Wood Awards
paragraphs: We are delighted to share that Streatham and Clapham High School has been shortlisted for this year’s Wood Awards. Selected within the Education and Public Sector category, the awards recognise, encourage and promote outstanding design, craftsmanship and installation using wood.

The shortlist will be showcased at the London Design Fair in the Old Truman Brewery on 20th-23rd September, with the winners revealed at the annual Wood Awards ceremony at Carpenters’ Hall on 20th November.

open-house-london-2018.title: Open House London 2018
paragraphs: We are pleased to have 3 projects included in Open House London this year.

If you would like to take a look inside some of the projects we have completed over the course of 2018 then please come and visit us on Saturday 22nd September, where we will be at Streatham and Clapham High School in Lambeth and at 25 Stories Mews in Southwark.
